subject: Food Science
title: Fat as Mouthfeel
description: A quick, practical guide to Fat as Mouthfeel.

hook.text: Fat as Mouthfeel: a surprising example shows why better reasoning matters.

buildup.text: Fat lubricates the mouth, reducing friction between food and oral surfaces. This creates the sensation of richness and smoothness.

discovery.text: Fat carries and slowly releases flavor compounds. Fat-soluble aromas linger longer in fatty foods.

twist.text: Low-fat products often compensate with sugar and thickeners to mimic fat's mouthfeel.

climax.text: Scientists are developing fat replacers—olestra, inulin, carrageenan—that mimic fat's texture without calories.

punchline.text: Fat's role goes beyond taste. It coats, lubricates, and extends flavor.

quiz.question: Why do low-fat products often have similar or more calories than full-fat versions?
options: Sugar and thickeners are added to compensate for the lost mouthfeel of fat
Fat has fewer calories than people think
